# fursy - AI Agent Guide

> **Module**: `github.com/coregx/fursy`
> **Go**: 1.27+ (generic methods on concrete types)
> **License**: MIT
> **Current version**: `CHANGELOG.md` is the source of truth. This repository may be ahead of the latest tag (the `Unreleased` section lists merged but unreleased work), so do not hardcode a version in code or docs.

This file is the public, machine-oriented guide to the fursy HTTP router. It describes the code in this repository, not a roadmap. Every API name and number below was checked against the source or produced by the commands shown next to it.

## Project Overview

fursy (Fast Universal Routing SYstem) is an HTTP router for Go 1.27+ with two handler styles:

- **Plain handlers** registered with `router.Handle(method, path, handler)`. They receive `*fursy.Context`.
- **Type-safe handlers** registered with `router.GET`, `router.POST`, `router.PUT`, `router.DELETE`, `router.PATCH`, `router.HEAD`, `router.OPTIONS`. They receive `*fursy.Box[Req, Res]`; Go 1.27 infers `Req` and `Res` from the handler signature.

The same split exists on `*RouteGroup`.

### Main capabilities

| Capability | Public API | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Radix tree routing | `Router.Handle`, `Router.GET`-style methods | Static, `:param`, and `*catchAll` segments. No regex constraints. |
| Type-safe request/response | `Box[Req, Res]`, `Handler[Req, Res]` | Request body is bound and optionally validated before the handler runs. |
| RFC 9457 errors | `Problem`, `NotFound`, `BadRequest`, `ValidationProblem`, ... | Default error format for router and middleware errors (`application/problem+json`). |
| OpenAPI 3.1 | `Router.GenerateOpenAPI`, `Router.ServeOpenAPI`, `RouteOptions` | Schemas inferred from `Box[Req, Res]`; named components and `$ref`; deterministic `operationId`. |
| Route groups | `Router.Group`, `RouteGroup.Group`, `RouteGroup.Use` | Nested prefixes and middleware inheritance. |
| Nine middleware | package `middleware` | Logger, Recovery, CORS, BasicAuth, JWT, RateLimit, CircuitBreaker, Secure, Timeout. |
| Content negotiation | `Context.Negotiate`, `Context.NegotiateFormat`, `Context.Accepts` | RFC 9110 quality values. `Negotiate` renders JSON, XML, and plain text. |
| API versioning | `Version`, `RequireVersion`, `DeprecateVersion`, `Context.APIVersion` | Header or URL-path version extraction; RFC 8594 deprecation headers. |
| Graceful shutdown | `OnShutdown`, `Shutdown`, `ListenAndServeWithShutdown`, `SetServer` | Drains connections, then runs callbacks in reverse order. |
| Body limits | `SetMaxBodySize`, `MaxBodySize` | Default 4 MiB; applies to plain and generic handlers. |
| Plugins | `plugins/validator`, `plugins/opentelemetry`, `plugins/stream`, `plugins/database` | Separate Go modules. |

### Dependencies

The root module requires only two external modules (`go.mod`):

- `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5` for JWT middleware.
- `golang.org/x/time` for rate limiting.

Routing, context, groups, errors, OpenAPI, negotiation, and the other seven middleware use the standard library.

The values below were produced in this checkout with Go 1.27.4 on Windows/amd64. Re-run the commands before quoting them; hardware and Go versions change nanoseconds.

```bash
go test -cover ./...
```

|---|---|
| `github.com/coregx/fursy` (root) | 94.0% |
| `github.com/coregx/fursy/internal/binding` | 93.5% |
| `github.com/coregx/fursy/internal/negotiate` | 88.0% |
| `github.com/coregx/fursy/internal/radix` | 89.0% |
| `github.com/coregx/fursy/middleware` | 95.6% |

Top-level test functions and benchmark/fuzz counts for the root module (plugins and examples are separate modules and are not included):

```bash
go test -list '^Test' ./... | grep -c '^Test'   # 501
grep -rh '^func Benchmark' --include='*_test.go' . | wc -l   # 22
grep -rh '^func Fuzz' --include='*_test.go' . | wc -l        # 2
```

The fuzz targets are `FuzzRadixLookup` and `FuzzRoutePattern` in `internal/radix`.

### Routing performance

```bash

```

Measured output (12th Gen Intel i7-1255U, Go 1.27.4):

```

BenchmarkRouter_ParameterRoute-12                   9155196    213.5 ns/op    0 B/op    0 allocs/op

```

The important invariant is **0 allocs/op** on these paths. Nanoseconds are environment-specific; never present them as a fixed guarantee.

## Repository Layout

```
fursy/
├── router.go              # Router: registration, lookup, ServeHTTP, shutdown
├── context.go             # Context: request/response helpers, params, middleware chain
├── box.go                 # Box[Req, Res]: type-safe context, binding, typed responses
├── handler_generic.go     # Handler[Req, Res] and the generic-to-plain adapter
├── group.go               # RouteGroup: prefixes, nested groups, middleware
├── problem.go             # RFC 9457 Problem and constructors
├── error.go               # Common HTTP error values
├── openapi.go             # OpenAPI 3.1 document and schema generation
├── route_info.go          # RouteInfo/RouteOptions metadata
├── validation.go          # Validator interface and ValidationErrors
├── version.go             # API version type, parsing, version middleware
├── middleware.go          # HandlerFunc and middleware chain types
├── mime.go                # MIME constants
├── empty.go               # Empty request/response marker type
│
├── internal/
│   ├── radix/             # Radix tree engine (tree.go, node.go)
│   ├── binding/           # Body binding (JSON, XML, form, multipart)
│   └── negotiate/         # Accept header parsing and q-value selection
│
├── middleware/            # Nine flat middleware implementations
│   ├── logger.go
│   ├── recovery.go
│   ├── cors.go
│   ├── basicauth.go
│   ├── jwt.go
│   ├── ratelimit.go
│   ├── circuitbreaker.go
│   ├── secure.go
│   └── timeout.go
│
├── plugins/               # Separate Go modules
│   ├── validator/
│   ├── opentelemetry/
│   ├── stream/
│   └── database/
│
├── examples/
│   ├── 01-hello-world/ ... 10-production-boilerplate/
│   └── validation/01-basic ... 06-production/
│
├── docs/PERFORMANCE.md
├── README.md
├── CHANGELOG.md
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── ROADMAP.md
├── SECURITY.md
├── llms.txt
└── go.mod
```

`docs/dev/`, `.claude/`, and `tmp/` are gitignored private directories. If present in a working checkout they may contain internal notes, but they are not part of the published repository. Do not link to them from public docs.

### Architecture rule

The root package is the public API and wraps `internal/`. External modules cannot import `github.com/coregx/fursy/internal/...`; only code inside the fursy module can. Keep implementation details behind the root package and the `middleware` package.

---

## Critical Files

Read these first when working on the repository:

1. `README.md` - user-facing overview and examples.
2. `CHANGELOG.md` - released and unreleased changes; the only authoritative version source.
3. `go.mod` - Go version and allowed core dependencies.
4. `CONTRIBUTING.md` - GitHub Flow, commit style, quality gates.
5. `llms.txt` - this guide.
6. `examples/` - runnable, copy-pasteable usage.
7. `plugins/*/README.md` - per-plugin APIs.
8. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` - benchmark narrative.

For the public API, prefer `go doc -all .`, `go doc ./middleware`, and `go doc ./internal/radix` over reading from memory.

## Quick Start

### Minimal application (plain handlers)

```go
package main

import (
    "log"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/coregx/fursy"
)

func main() {
    router := fursy.New()

    router.Handle("GET", "/", func(c *fursy.Context) error {
        return c.Text("Hello, fursy!")
    })

    router.Handle("GET", "/users/:id", func(c *fursy.Context) error {
        return c.OK(map[string]string{"id": c.Param("id")})
    })

    log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", router))
}
```

`router.Handle` (and `router.HandleWithOptions`) accept a plain `fursy.HandlerFunc`. The uppercase generic methods accept only `fursy.Handler[Req, Res]`.

### Type-safe handlers with automatic binding

```go
package main

import (
    "log"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/coregx/fursy"
)

type CreateUserRequest struct {
    Name  string `json:"name" validate:"required,min=3"`
    Email string `json:"email" validate:"required,email"`
}

type UserResponse struct {
    ID    string `json:"id"`
    Name  string `json:"name"`
    Email string `json:"email"`
}

func createUser(req *CreateUserRequest) UserResponse {
    return UserResponse{ID: "1", Name: req.Name, Email: req.Email}
}

func main() {
    router := fursy.New()

    router.POST("/users", func(c *fursy.Box[CreateUserRequest, UserResponse]) error {
        // c.ReqBody is already bound (and validated if a validator is configured).
        user := createUser(c.ReqBody)
        return c.Created("/users/"+user.ID, user)
    })

    log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", router))
}
```

### Router with middleware and OpenAPI

```go
package main

import (
    "log"
    "net/http"
    "time"

    "github.com/coregx/fursy"
    "github.com/coregx/fursy/middleware"
)

type CreateUserRequest struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
}

type UserResponse struct {
    ID   string `json:"id"`
    Name string `json:"name"`
}

func main() {
    router := fursy.New()

    router.WithInfo(fursy.Info{
        Title:   "Users API",
        Version: "1.0.0",
    })

    router.Use(
        middleware.Recovery(),
        middleware.Logger(),
        middleware.CORS(),
        middleware.Secure(),
        middleware.Timeout(5*time.Second),
    )

    router.POST("/users", func(c *fursy.Box[CreateUserRequest, UserResponse]) error {
        return c.Created("/users/1", UserResponse{ID: "1", Name: c.ReqBody.Name})
    }, &fursy.RouteOptions{
        Summary:       "Create user",
        Tags:          []string{"users"},
        SuccessStatus: http.StatusCreated,
    })

    router.ServeOpenAPI("/openapi.json")

    log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", router))
}
```

The ordering above follows the middleware rules in [Middleware](#middleware): `Recovery` and `Logger` wrap everything; `CORS` and `Secure` run before `Timeout` so their headers survive a timeout response.

---

## Core Concepts

### Plain handlers vs typed handlers

| | Plain | Typed |
|---|---|---|
| Registration | `router.Handle("GET", path, fn)` | `router.GET(path, fn)` |
| Handler type | `fursy.HandlerFunc` (`func(*Context) error`) | `fursy.Handler[Req, Res]` (`func(*Box[Req, Res]) error`) |
| Context | `*fursy.Context` | `*fursy.Box[Req, Res]` (embeds `*Context`) |
| Body binding | Manual (decode `c.Request.Body` yourself) | Automatic before the handler runs |
| Validation | Manual | Automatic when `SetValidator` is configured |
| OpenAPI types | Not inferred | `Req` and `Res` inferred from the handler |

`router.GET("/path", func(c *fursy.Context) error { ... })` does not compile: the generic methods require a `Handler[Req, Res]`. Use `Handle` for plain handlers.

### Box and automatic binding

```go
type Box[Req, Res any] struct {
    *Context

    ReqBody *Req // parsed, optionally validated request body
    ResBody *Res // response body set by the typed response helpers
}
```

`adaptGenericHandler` (in `handler_generic.go`) creates the box and calls `Bind()` before invoking the handler. `Box.Bind` is idempotent: if `ReqBody` is already set it returns nil without re-reading the body.

Supported request content types (`internal/binding`):

- `application/json` (also used when `Content-Type` is empty)
- `application/xml`, `text/xml`
- `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
- `multipart/form-data`

Only the request body is bound. URL parameters, query values, and headers are read through `Context` methods, not through struct tags.

### The Empty marker

Use `fursy.Empty` when there is no request or response body:

```go
type DeleteRequest struct {
    ID string
}

router.DELETE("/users/:id", func(c *fursy.Box[fursy.Empty, fursy.Empty]) error {
    deleteUser(c.Param("id"))
    return c.NoContentSuccess() // 204
})
```

`Empty` tells `Bind` to skip body parsing and tells OpenAPI that there is no request/response schema. A non-empty `Req` type requires a body; an empty body returns a 400 Problem.

### Route groups

```go
api := router.Group("/api/v1")
api.Use(middleware.Logger())

admin := api.Group("/admin", middleware.JWT(secretBytes))
admin.GET("/users", listUsers)
```

Middleware order is `Router.Use()` -> parent group middleware -> child group middleware -> handler. Groups can nest arbitrarily.

### Middleware pipeline

Middleware and handlers share the `HandlerFunc` signature:

```go
func MyMiddleware() fursy.HandlerFunc {
    return func(c *fursy.Context) error {
        start := time.Now()
        err := c.Next() // run the rest of the chain
        slog.Info("request", "method", c.Request.Method, "duration", time.Since(start))
        return err
    }
}
```

- `c.Next()` executes the next handler and returns its error.
- `c.Abort()` prevents subsequent handlers from running; it does not stop the current handler.
- `c.IsAborted()` reports whether the chain was aborted.
- Middleware that forgets `c.Next()` silently skips the rest of the chain. The route handler never runs and the client receives an empty 200.

### Context pooling

`Context` objects come from a `sync.Pool` and are reset after each request (`Router.ServeHTTP`). Never retain a `*Context` or `*Box` beyond the handler call, and never use one from a goroutine that outlives the request. This is why the Timeout middleware is cooperative instead of running handlers in another goroutine.

### Convenience response methods

`Context` (and therefore `Box`, which embeds it):

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| `OK(obj)` | 200 with JSON body |
| `Created(obj)` | 201 with JSON body (no `Location` header) |
| `Accepted(obj)` | 202 with JSON body |
| `NoContent(code)` | status with no body |
| `NoContentSuccess()` | 204 |
| `Text(s)` | 200 `text/plain` |
| `String(code, s)` | status `text/plain` |
| `JSON(code, obj)` | status `application/json` |
| `JSONIndent(code, obj, indent)` | pretty JSON |
| `XML(code, obj)` | status `application/xml` |
| `Blob(code, contentType, data)` | binary body |
| `Stream(code, contentType, reader)` | stream from `io.Reader` |
| `Markdown(content)` | 200 `text/markdown` |
| `Redirect(code, url)` | 3xx redirect (3xx only) |
| `SetHeader(key, value)` | response header before writing |
| `GetHeader(key)` | request header |
| `Param(name)`, `Query(name)`, `QueryDefault`, `QueryValues`, `Form`, `FormDefault`, `PostForm` | request data |
| `Set(key, value)`, `Get`, `GetString`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` | per-request middleware data |
| `RoutePattern()` | registered pattern such as `/users/:id` |
| `APIVersion()` | version from `Api-Version` header or URL path |

`Box` typed response helpers: `OK`, `Created(location, data)`, `Accepted`, `UpdatedOK`, `NoContentSuccess`, `UpdatedNoContent`, `BadRequest`, `Unauthorized`, `Forbidden`, `NotFound`, `InternalServerError`.

Note that `Box.BadRequest(data)` and its siblings write a normal JSON body of type `Res`; they are not RFC 9457 Problems. Return a `fursy.Problem` (or use `Context.Problem`) when you want the standard error format.

### Route patterns

Supported patterns:

- Static: `/users`, `/files/report.pdf`
- Named parameter: `/users/:id` (read with `c.Param("id")`)
- Catch-all: `/files/*path` (must be the last segment; read with `c.Param("path")`)

Colons are only special at the start of a segment. Mid-segment colons are literal, which enables AIP-136 custom methods such as `/documents:commit`. There is no regex constraint syntax.

Duplicate registration panics (`route already exists: ...`), as do empty methods/paths and nil handlers.

Trailing slashes are significant by default. Configure with `router.WithTrailingSlash(...)`:

- `fursy.IgnoreTrailingSlash` (default): `/users` and `/users/` are different routes.
- `fursy.StripTrailingSlash`: serve the canonical handler without a redirect.
- `fursy.RedirectTrailingSlash`: bidirectional redirect, 301 for GET and 308 for other methods.

### HEAD and OPTIONS

- A HEAD request falls back to the matching GET route (RFC 9110), without a body.
- An OPTIONS request to a path registered for other methods returns 204 with an `Allow` header.
- A known path with the wrong method returns 405 with an `Allow` header and an RFC 9457 body.

### Graceful shutdown

```go
router.OnShutdown(func() {
    db.Close()
})

if err := router.ListenAndServeWithShutdown(":8080", 25*time.Second); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
```

`ListenAndServeWithShutdown` listens for SIGTERM/SIGINT, drains connections with the given timeout (default 30s), then runs callbacks in reverse registration order. `Shutdown(ctx)` is idempotent. `SetServer(*http.Server)` attaches an externally created server. Do not confuse `SetServer(*http.Server)` with `WithServer(fursy.Server)`, which only adds a URL to the OpenAPI document.

### API versioning

```go
version := c.APIVersion() // Api-Version header first, then /v1/, /v2/, ...

v1 := router.Group("/api/v1")
v1.Use(fursy.RequireVersion(fursy.Version{Major: 1}))
v1.Use(fursy.DeprecateVersion(fursy.DeprecationInfo{
    Version: fursy.Version{Major: 1},
    Message: "Migrate to v2",
}))

v1.Use(fursy.RequireVersion(fursy.Version{Major: 2}))
```

`ParseVersion` accepts `v1`, `v2.1`, `v3.2.1`, `1`, `2.1.0`. `ExtractVersionFromPath` recognizes `/v1/...` and `/api/v2.1/...`.

---

## Routing API

### Router methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fursy.New()` | Create a router with pooling, 405 handling, OPTIONS handling, and a 4 MiB body limit. |
| `Handle(method, path, HandlerFunc)` | Register a plain handler. |
| `HandleWithOptions(method, path, HandlerFunc, *RouteOptions)` | Plain handler plus OpenAPI metadata. |
| `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS(path, Handler[Req,Res], ...*RouteOptions)` | Register a typed handler. |
| `Use(...HandlerFunc)` | Append global middleware. |
| `Group(prefix, ...HandlerFunc)` | Create a route group. |
| `WithInfo(Info)` | Set OpenAPI `info`. |
| `WithServer(Server)` | Add an OpenAPI server URL. |
| `ServeOpenAPI(path)` | Register a JSON OpenAPI endpoint. |
| `GenerateOpenAPI(Info) (*OpenAPI, error)` | Build the document in memory. |
| `WithTrailingSlash(TrailingSlashBehavior)` | Configure trailing-slash handling. |
| `SetValidator(Validator)` | Enable automatic validation during `Box.Bind`. |
| `SetErrorHandler(ErrorHandler)` | Replace default error classification. |
| `SetErrorLogger(func(error, *http.Request))` | Observe unclassified 500 errors. |
| `SetMaxBodySize(int64)` | Change the body limit; 0 disables it. |
| `MaxBodySize() int64` | Read the current limit. |
| `SetServer(*http.Server)` | Attach a server for shutdown. |
| `OnShutdown(func())` | Register a shutdown callback. |
| `Shutdown(context.Context) error` | Drain and run callbacks. |
| `ListenAndServeWithShutdown(addr, ...time.Duration) error` | Serve until SIGTERM/SIGINT. |

`RouteGroup` exposes the same typed verbs plus `Handle`, `HandleWithOptions`, `Use`, `Group`, and typed verbs taking `...*RouteOptions`.

### RouteOptions

```go
type RouteOptions struct {
    Summary             string
    Description         string
    Tags                []string
    OperationID         string
    Deprecated          bool
    Parameters          []RouteParameter
    Responses           map[int]RouteResponse
    SuccessStatus       int
    OptionalRequestBody bool
}
```

---

## Request Binding and Validation

### Automatic binding

For typed handlers only, the adapter calls `Bind()` before the handler:

1. `Req == fursy.Empty` -> skip.
2. Choose a binder from `Content-Type`.
3. Decode the body into a new `Req`.
4. If `router.SetValidator` was called, validate the struct.
5. Assign `c.ReqBody`.

A body is required for non-`Empty` request types. For example, `Box[GetUserRequest, UserResponse]` on a GET without a body returns 400; use `Box[fursy.Empty, UserResponse]` and read `c.Param("id")`.

`Bind()` is idempotent, so calling it manually is harmless but unnecessary.

### Validation

```go
import "github.com/coregx/fursy/plugins/validator"

router.SetValidator(validator.New())
```

`fursy.Validator` is a one-method interface:

```go
type Validator interface {
    Validate(any) error
}
```

The plugin uses `validate:"..."` tags from go-playground/validator. Validation failures become `fursy.ValidationErrors`; the default error handler converts them to a 422 RFC 9457 response with an `errors` extension mapping field names to messages:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Validation Failed",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "One or more fields failed validation",
  "errors": {
    "email": "must be a valid email address"
  }
}
```

Validation applies to the bound body struct only. Query parameters, path parameters, and headers are not validated automatically; validate them in the handler and return a `Problem` or `ValidationErrors` yourself.

### Body size limit

`New()` sets a 4 MiB (`4 << 20`) global limit. `ServeHTTP` wraps the body in `http.MaxBytesReader` for every handler, plain or typed. Oversized bodies produce a 413 Problem. `SetMaxBodySize(0)` disables the limit.

---

## Error Handling with RFC 9457

RFC 9457 Problem Details is the default error format. `Problem` marshals to `application/problem+json`:

```go
type Problem struct {
    Type       string         `json:"type"`
    Title      string         `json:"title"`
    Status     int            `json:"status"`
    Detail     string         `json:"detail,omitempty"`
    Instance   string         `json:"instance,omitempty"`
    Extensions map[string]any `json:"-"`
}
```

Extension fields are flattened into the JSON object. Constructors: `NewProblem`, `BadRequest`, `Unauthorized`, `Forbidden`, `NotFound`, `MethodNotAllowed`, `Conflict`, `UnprocessableEntity`, `TooManyRequests`, `InternalServerError`, `ServiceUnavailable`, `NotAcceptable`, `ValidationProblem`.

### Default error classification

`defaultErrorHandler` maps errors as follows:

| Error | Response |
|---|---|
| `Problem` | Its `Status`, same Problem body |
| `ValidationErrors` | 422 with `errors` extension |
| `*http.MaxBytesError` | 413 |
| `binding.ErrUnsupportedMediaType` | 415 |
| `binding.ErrEmptyRequestBody` | 400 |
| `*binding.DecodeError` (JSON/XML) | 400 |
| Anything else | 500; logged through `SetErrorLogger`, details hidden |

Router-generated errors use the same format: 404, 405 (+ `Allow`), 400/413/415 from binding, and 500.

Custom handling:

```go
router.SetErrorHandler(func(c *fursy.Context, err error) {
    var problem fursy.Problem
    if errors.As(err, &problem) {
        _ = c.Problem(problem.WithInstance(c.Request.URL.Path))
        return
    }
    _ = c.Problem(fursy.InternalServerError("internal error"))
})
```

`SetErrorLogger(func(err error, req *http.Request))` fires only for unclassified errors that become 500; Problems, validation errors, decode errors, and body-limit errors are handled before that point.

---

## OpenAPI 3.1 Generation

### Setup

```go
router := fursy.New()

router.WithInfo(fursy.Info{
    Title:       "Users API",
    Version:     "1.0.0",
    Description: "Example API",
})
router.WithServer(fursy.Server{
    URL:         "https://api.example.com",
    Description: "Production",
})

router.POST("/users", createUser, &fursy.RouteOptions{
    Summary:             "Create user",
    Tags:                []string{"users"},
    SuccessStatus:       http.StatusCreated,
    OptionalRequestBody: false,
})

router.ServeOpenAPI("/openapi.json")
```

`ServeOpenAPI` regenerates the document on every request. For production, call `GenerateOpenAPI` once and serve the cached result, or serve a pre-generated file.

### What is inferred

- Request and response schemas from `Box[Req, Res]` types.
- Named package types are registered once in `components.schemas` and referenced with `$ref`; recursive and mutually recursive types terminate.
- Strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, maps, structs, embedded structs, and JSON tags.
- `time.Time` -> `{"type":"string","format":"date-time"}`.
- `[]byte` and named byte slices -> `{"type":"string","format":"byte"}`.
- `json.RawMessage` -> `{}` (unconstrained).
- `:id` and `*path` templates -> required `in: path` parameters.
- `operationId` from method + path when not set explicitly, for example `GET /users/:id` -> `getUsersById`; collisions get a numeric suffix.
- A 400 and a 500 response referencing the `Problem` schema, unless the route already declares those status codes.

### Status codes and bodies

- `RouteOptions.SuccessStatus` sets the inferred success status; 0 means "choose from the response type".
- 204 emits no response body.
- A route with no inferred response type infers 204. This includes `Res == fursy.Empty` **and plain handlers registered with `Handle`/`HandleWithOptions`**, which have no response type. Set `SuccessStatus` to override (for example, 200 for a plain handler that writes JSON).
- `OptionalRequestBody: true` marks the inferred request body as not required.
- Explicit `RouteOptions.Responses` are merged with the inferred success response. A custom 404 does not remove the inferred 200. An explicit entry with the same status code replaces the inferred one for that status.
- Without `ContentType`, explicit responses default to `application/json` for 2xx and `application/problem+json` for 4xx and above.

### Document output

`GenerateOpenAPI` returns `*OpenAPI`. `WriteJSON(w)` and `WriteYAML(w)` serialize it. `ServeOpenAPI(path)` registers a GET route that writes JSON.

OpenAPI generation uses metadata captured at registration. Routes registered with plain `Handle` have no request/response types, so annotate them with `HandleWithOptions` and `RouteOptions.Parameters`/`Responses` when the document matters.

---

## Middleware

The `middleware` package contains nine implementations. Only JWT and RateLimit add external dependencies.

| Middleware | Constructor | Dependency | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Logger | `Logger()`, `LoggerWithConfig` | stdlib `log/slog` | Structured request logging; `SkipPaths`, `SkipFunc`. |
| Recovery | `Recovery()`, `RecoveryWithConfig` | none | Recovers panics, logs stack, returns a 500 Problem. |
| CORS | `CORS()`, `CORSWithConfig` | none | Preflight and actual-request CORS headers. |
| BasicAuth | `BasicAuth(ValidatorFunc)`, `BasicAuthAccounts`, `BasicAuthWithConfig` | none | HTTP Basic authentication; stores identity under `UserContextKey` (`"User"`). |
| JWT | `JWT(key)`, `JWTWithConfig` | `golang-jwt/jwt/v5` | Bearer token validation; stores claims under `JWTContextKey` (`"jwt"`) and the raw token under `JWTTokenContextKey` (`"jwt_token"`). |
| RateLimit | `RateLimit(rate, burst)`, `RateLimitWithConfig` | `golang.org/x/time` | Token bucket per key; `X-RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After`; 429 Problem. |
| CircuitBreaker | `CircuitBreaker()`, `CircuitBreakerConsecutive`, `CircuitBreakerRatio`, `CircuitBreakerTimeWindow`, `CircuitBreakerWithConfig`, `CircuitBreakerWithName` | none | Closed/Open/Half-Open states; 503 Problem when open; 4xx Problems do not trip it. |
| Secure | `Secure()`, `SecureWithConfig`, `SecureDefaults`, `SecureStrict`, `SecureWithCSP`, `SecureWithHSTS` | none | OWASP-style security headers. |
| Timeout | `Timeout(d)`, `TimeoutWithConfig` | none | Cooperative context deadline; 503 Problem on timeout; `ErrRequestTimeout` cause. |

### Ordering rules

1. `Recovery` should wrap everything so panics in other middleware are caught.
2. `Logger` should run early so it sees all traffic, including 404/405 responses (the router runs global middleware for those).
3. `CORS` must be registered globally with `router.Use()`, not on a group, and before authentication. Preflight OPTIONS requests carry no credentials; if JWT or BasicAuth runs first, the preflight receives 401 instead of CORS headers.
4. Middleware that sets response headers (`CORS`, `Secure`, request-ID middleware) must be registered **before** `Timeout`. When a timeout produces a 503, the middleware restores the header snapshot taken before the inner chain ran; headers set inside the timeout are discarded with the handler's headers.
5. Apply `Timeout` per group when different routes need different limits. Deadlines can only shrink; a nested Timeout cannot extend an outer one.

A safe global order:

```go
router.Use(
    middleware.Recovery(),
    middleware.Logger(),
    middleware.CORS(),
    middleware.Secure(),
    middleware.Timeout(5*time.Second),
)
```

### Logger

```go
router.Use(middleware.Logger())
router.Use(middleware.LoggerWithConfig(middleware.LoggerConfig{
    Logger:    slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stdout, nil)),
    SkipPaths: []string{"/health", "/metrics"},
}))
```

### Recovery

```go
router.Use(middleware.Recovery())
```

Panics become a 500 Problem. `RecoveryConfig` controls the logger, stack-trace printing, and buffer size. `PanicHandler()` is available as a lower-level alternative and re-panics `http.ErrAbortHandler`, matching net/http expectations.

### CORS

`CORSConfig` fields are comma-separated strings, not slices:

```go
router.Use(middleware.CORSWithConfig(middleware.CORSConfig{
    AllowOrigins:     "https://app.example.com",
    AllowMethods:     "GET,POST,PUT,DELETE,OPTIONS",
    AllowHeaders:     "Content-Type,Authorization",
    ExposeHeaders:    "X-Request-ID",
    AllowCredentials: true,
    MaxAge:           12 * time.Hour,
}))
```

Defaults: `AllowOrigins: "*"`, `AllowMethods: "GET,HEAD,PUT,POST,DELETE,PATCH"`, `AllowHeaders: "Content-Type,Accept,Authorization"`. `AllowOrigins: "null"` disallows all origins. `AllowOrigins: "*"` together with `AllowCredentials: true` panics, because it would reflect any origin with credentials. Register globally.

### BasicAuth

```go
router.Use(middleware.BasicAuth(middleware.BasicAuthAccounts(map[string]string{
    "admin": "secret",
})))

// Or a custom validator:
router.Use(middleware.BasicAuth(func(c *fursy.Context, username, password string) (any, error) {
    if username == "admin" && password == "secret" {
        return "admin", nil
    }
    return nil, fursy.ErrUnauthorized
}))
```

`BasicAuthWithConfig` supports `Realm`, `Validator`, and `Skipper`. The identity is stored under `middleware.UserContextKey` and is read with `c.Get(...)` or `c.GetString(...)` when it is a string.

### JWT

```go
router.Use(middleware.JWTWithConfig(middleware.JWTConfig{
    SigningKey:    []byte("secret"),
    SigningMethod: "HS256",
}))

router.Handle("GET", "/me", func(c *fursy.Context) error {
    claims := c.Get(middleware.JWTContextKey) // jwt.MapClaims by default
    return c.OK(claims)
})
```

Default token lookup is `header:Authorization` with the `Bearer` scheme. `JWTConfig` supports `TokenLookup` (`header:`, `query:`, `cookie:`), custom `Claims`, issuer/audience validation, and `ErrorHandler`. Always set `SigningMethod` explicitly to prevent algorithm-confusion attacks. `JWTHelper{}.GenerateToken(claims, key, method)` creates tokens for tests.

### RateLimit

```go
router.Use(middleware.RateLimit(10, 20)) // 10 req/s, burst 20

router.Use(middleware.RateLimitWithConfig(middleware.RateLimitConfig{
    Rate:  100,
    Burst: 200,
    KeyFunc: func(c *fursy.Context) string {
        return c.GetString("user_id")
    },
}))
```

Defaults: `Rate` 10 req/s, `Burst` `max(1, 2*Rate)`, key from `RemoteAddr` (proxy headers are not trusted by default). `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` are set unless `NoHeaders` is true. Exceeding the limit returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Use `NewRateLimiter(config)` when you need `Stop()` to release the cleanup goroutine.

### CircuitBreaker

```go
router.Use(middleware.CircuitBreaker()) // 5 consecutive failures, 60s open
router.Use(middleware.CircuitBreakerConsecutive(5, 30*time.Second))
router.Use(middleware.CircuitBreakerRatio(3, 10, 30*time.Second))
router.Use(middleware.CircuitBreakerWithConfig(middleware.CircuitBreakerConfig{
    ConsecutiveFailures: 5,
    Timeout:             30 * time.Second,
    MaxRequests:         2,
}))
```

States: `StateClosed`, `StateOpen`, `StateHalfOpen`. A 4xx `Problem` is treated as a client outcome and does not trip the breaker; 5xx and transport errors do. When open, requests receive a 503 Problem.

### Secure

```go
router.Use(middleware.Secure())
router.Use(middleware.SecureWithConfig(middleware.SecureWithHSTS(31536000, false)))
router.Use(middleware.SecureWithConfig(middleware.SecureWithCSP("default-src 'self'")))
```

`SecureDefaults()` sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. HSTS, CSP, COEP/COOP/CORP, and Permissions-Policy require explicit configuration. `SecureStrict()` enables a strict production profile and may break inline scripts or cross-origin resources.

### Timeout

```go
router.Use(middleware.Timeout(5 * time.Second))

router.Use(middleware.TimeoutWithConfig(middleware.TimeoutConfig{
    Timeout: 2 * time.Second,
    Skipper: func(c *fursy.Context) bool {
        return strings.HasPrefix(c.Request.URL.Path, "/events")
    },
    ErrorHandler: func(_ *fursy.Context, _ error) error {
        return fursy.NewProblem(http.StatusGatewayTimeout, "Gateway Timeout", "")
    },
}))
```

Behavior:

- Adds a deadline to `c.Request.Context()` with cause `middleware.ErrRequestTimeout`.
- Runs the handler synchronously. No extra goroutine, so pooled `Context` objects are safe.
- If the handler returns an error wrapping `context.DeadlineExceeded` or `ErrRequestTimeout` before writing a response, the middleware restores the pre-chain headers and returns 503 by default.
- Written responses, `nil`, and unrelated errors pass through unchanged. Client disconnects and shorter parent deadlines are not reported as timeouts.
- `DefaultTimeout` is 30s when the configured value is zero or negative.
- Preserves `http.Flusher` and `http.Hijacker`.
- Keep `http.Server` timeouts (`ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`); the request context does not bound body reads or response writes. Set `WriteTimeout` longer than the middleware timeout.

Use `Skipper` for SSE, WebSocket, and other long-lived routes.

---

## Plugins

Plugins are separate Go modules with their own `go.mod`, pinned to a released fursy version. Import paths:

```go
import "github.com/coregx/fursy/plugins/validator"
import "github.com/coregx/fursy/plugins/opentelemetry"
import "github.com/coregx/fursy/plugins/stream"
import "github.com/coregx/fursy/plugins/database"
```

### validator

Implements `fursy.Validator` with go-playground/validator/v10.

```go
router.SetValidator(validator.New())

// Custom rules:
v := validator.New()
v.RegisterAlias("username", "required,min=3,max=50")
v.RegisterCustomValidator("even", func(fl validator.FieldLevel) bool {
    return fl.Field().Int()%2 == 0
})
router.SetValidator(v)
```

API: `New(opts ...*Options)`, `DefaultOptions()`, `Struct`, `Validate`, `Var`, `RegisterAlias`, `RegisterCustomValidator`, `RegisterTagNameFunc`.

### opentelemetry

Tracing and metrics with the OpenTelemetry SDK.

```go
router.Use(opentelemetry.Middleware("my-service"))
router.Use(opentelemetry.Metrics("my-service"))

// Configured variants:
router.Use(opentelemetry.MiddlewareWithConfig(opentelemetry.Config{ /* ... */ }))
router.Use(opentelemetry.MetricsWithConfig(opentelemetry.MetricsConfig{ /* ... */ }))
```

Spans use `Context.RoutePattern()` for the `http.route` attribute, so labels stay low-cardinality.

### stream

SSE and WebSocket support built on `github.com/coregx/stream`.

```go
hub := sse.NewHub[Notification]()
go hub.Run()
defer hub.Close()

router.Use(stream.SSEHub(hub))
router.Handle("GET", "/events", func(c *fursy.Context) error {
    h, _ := stream.GetSSEHub[Notification](c)
    return stream.SSEUpgrade(c, func(conn *sse.Conn) error {
        h.Register(conn)
        defer h.Unregister(conn)
        <-conn.Done()
        return nil
    })
})
```

WebSocket equivalents: `stream.WebSocketHub(hub)`, `stream.GetWebSocketHub(c)`, `stream.WebSocketUpgrade(c, handler, opts)`. Long-lived upgrade routes should be excluded from `Timeout` with `Skipper`.

### database

Wraps `database/sql` and shares a connection or transaction through the request context.

```go
db := database.NewDB(sqlDB)
router.Use(database.Middleware(db))

router.Handle("GET", "/users/:id", func(c *fursy.Context) error {
    d, ok := database.GetDB(c)
    if !ok {
        return c.Problem(fursy.InternalServerError("database not configured"))
    }
    // d.QueryRow(c.Request.Context(), ...)
    return c.OK(user)
})
```

API: `NewDB`, `Middleware`, `TxMiddleware`, `WithTx`, `GetDB`, `GetDBOrError`, `MustGetDB`, `GetTx`, `GetTxOrError`, `MustGetTx`, `DB.DB`, `DB.BeginTx`, `DB.Exec`, `DB.Query`, `DB.QueryRow`, `DB.Ping`, `DB.Close`, and the same query methods on `*Tx` plus `Commit`/`Rollback`.

---

## Examples

Each runnable example (the ten numbered examples and the six validation examples) is a separate Go module with `go 1.27` and a local `replace` back to this checkout (the relative path depends on nesting depth). Run an example from its own directory:

```bash
cd examples/01-hello-world
go run .
```

| Example | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `01-hello-world` | Minimal router with a single GET endpoint and JSON response. |
| `02-rest-api-crud` | Full CRUD API with typed handlers and RFC 9457 errors. |
| `03-rest-api-with-openapi` | Generated OpenAPI: schemas and `$ref`, success statuses, groups, deprecation. |
| `04-content-negotiation` | JSON, XML, HTML, Markdown, and plain-text responses; q-values; `Accepts`/`AcceptsAny`. |
| `05-middleware` | Built-in middleware, custom middleware patterns, ordering, groups, auth. |
| `06-opentelemetry` | Tracing and metrics with Jaeger and Prometheus configuration. |
| `07-sse-notifications` | Server-Sent Events through `plugins/stream`. |
| `08-websocket-chat` | WebSocket chat through `plugins/stream`. |
| `09-rest-api-with-db` | SQL CRUD with `plugins/database`, transactions, and `WithTx`. |
| `10-production-boilerplate` | Production-style DDD API with fursy and stream; `cmd/`, `internal/`, migrations, Docker. |
| `validation/01-basic` | Minimal validator plugin setup. |
| `validation/02-rest-api-crud` | CRUD with validation. |
| `validation/03-custom-validator` | Custom rules and aliases. |
| `validation/04-nested-structs` | Nested struct validation. |
| `validation/05-custom-messages` | Custom error messages. |
| `validation/06-production` | Validation plus JWT, logging, and production setup. |

The `10-production-boilerplate` example additionally uses `github.com/coregx/stream`; see its `go.mod` for the exact versions.

## Testing and Quality Gates

### Commands

```bash
# All tests
go test ./...

# Race detector (CI and pull-request requirement)
go test -race ./...

# Coverage report
go test -coverprofile=coverage.txt ./...
go tool cover -func=coverage.txt | tail -1

# Focused test
go test -run TestName ./...

# Benchmarks
go test -bench=. -benchmem ./...

# Lint (must report no issues)
golangci-lint run

# Formatting check (must print nothing)
gofmt -l .
```

### Project requirements

`CONTRIBUTING.md` requires, for a pull request:

- Formatted code (`gofmt -l .` empty).
- `golangci-lint run` clean.
- All tests pass with `go test -race ./...`.
- New code has tests.
- Benchmarks for performance-critical code.
- Documentation updated when applicable; released changes are recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Conventional Commits.
- No external dependencies in the core package.

The repository's current measured coverage is in [Measured Repository State](#measured-repository-state). Do not lower it to make a change pass; add tests for the new behavior.

Plugins and examples are separate Go modules. `go test ./...` at the repository root covers the root module only; run plugin tests from each `plugins/*/` directory.

### Test style

Tests use table-driven subtests (`tests := []struct{...}` plus `t.Run`). Benchmarks call `b.ReportAllocs()`. Fuzz targets live beside the code they exercise. Race-detector runs are expected in CI; do not claim a change is verified if only `go build` was run.

---

## Git and Contribution Workflow

`CONTRIBUTING.md` defines GitHub Flow:

```
main                  # production-ready, tagged releases
  ├── feat/*          # features
  ├── fix/*           # bug fixes
  └── chore/*         # maintenance
```

Rules:

- `main` is the only long-lived branch. All pull requests target `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`; use a pull request.
- Small self-contained changes may be one commit; larger features use a feature branch.
- Conventional Commits: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, optionally with a scope.
- Keep commit messages professional and focused on the change.
- Semantic versioning: `0.y.0` for features, `0.y.z` for fixes before 1.0; major/minor/patch after 1.0. Breaking changes are allowed in 0.x releases.

Released versions are recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`; tags and releases are created by maintainers (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

---

## Common Gotchas

1. **`router.GET` needs a generic handler.** `router.GET(path, func(c *fursy.Context) error {...})` does not compile. Use `router.Handle("GET", path, fn)` for plain handlers.

2. **Automatic binding is only for `Box[Req, Res]`.** Plain handlers decode the body themselves. `Box.Bind` is called by the adapter and is idempotent; there is no need to call it manually.

3. **`Req` is the body type, not params/query.** `fursy.Box[GetUserRequest, Res]` on a GET expects a request body. For routes without a body, use `fursy.Box[fursy.Empty, Res]` and read `c.Param(...)` / `c.Query(...)`. Struct tags for binding are `json`, `xml`, and `form`; `param` and `query` tags are not interpreted.

4. **Never retain the Context.** Contexts and boxes come from a pool and are reset after `ServeHTTP`. Do not store them, and do not touch them from a goroutine that outlives the request.

5. **Timeout is cooperative.** It sets a context deadline; it does not kill the handler. Long-running work must pass `c.Request.Context()` to database drivers and HTTP clients, or select on `ctx.Done()`. Use `Skipper` for SSE/WebSocket routes.

6. **CORS/Secure before Timeout.** Timeout restores the header snapshot taken before the inner chain runs; headers set by middleware inside Timeout are discarded on a 503.

7. **CORS is global, not per-group.** Preflight OPTIONS requests are handled by the router before group middleware. Register `CORS` with `router.Use()` and before JWT/BasicAuth.

8. **The body limit is 4 MiB for all handlers.** `SetMaxBodySize` applies to plain and typed handlers; `0` disables it. Oversized bodies get 413.

9. **Validation needs `SetValidator`.** Without a validator, binding still happens but no `validate` tags run. Validation covers the body struct only.

10. **OpenAPI infers 204 for routes with no response type.** This includes `Box[Req, Empty]` and plain handlers. Set `RouteOptions.SuccessStatus` when a plain handler returns a body (for example, 200).

11. **`WithServer` is not `SetServer`.** `WithServer(fursy.Server)` adds a URL to the OpenAPI document. `SetServer(*http.Server)` attaches the real HTTP server for graceful shutdown.

12. **Duplicate routes panic.** Registering the same method and path twice panics with `route already exists`. So do empty methods/paths and nil handlers.

13. **No regex constraints.** Only static segments, `:param`, and trailing `*catchAll` are supported. Mid-segment colons are literal (AIP-136).

14. **JWT signing method must be explicit in production.** `JWTConfig.SigningMethod` defaults to `HS256`; set it to the expected algorithm so tokens signed with another algorithm are rejected.

15. **Rate limiting defaults to `RemoteAddr`.** `X-Forwarded-For` is not trusted by default. If you run behind a trusted proxy, set `KeyFunc` and validate the proxy yourself.

16. **Negotiate does not render Markdown or HTML.** `Context.Negotiate` offers JSON, XML, and plain text. Use `c.Accepts(fursy.MIMETextMarkdown)` plus `c.Markdown(...)` for Markdown, and write the HTML body yourself.

17. **Keep `http.Server` timeouts.** The Timeout middleware bounds handler work via the request context, not socket reads/writes. Configure `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, and `WriteTimeout` separately.

18. **`internal/` is not importable.** External modules must use the root package and `middleware`; `internal/radix`, `internal/binding`, and `internal/negotiate` are implementation details.

## Key Files Reference

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `router.go` | `Router`, registration, lookup, `ServeHTTP`, 404/405/OPTIONS, error dispatch, shutdown. |
| `context.go` | `Context`, params, query/form, response helpers, middleware chain, version access. |
| `box.go` | `Box[Req, Res]`, `Bind`, typed response helpers. |
| `handler_generic.go` | `Handler[Req, Res]`, `adaptGenericHandler`, empty-type detection. |
| `group.go` | `RouteGroup`, nested prefixes, group middleware, typed verbs. |
| `problem.go` | `Problem`, constructors, extension flattening, `ValidationProblem`. |
| `validation.go` | `Validator`, `ValidationError(s)`, field maps. |
| `openapi.go` | Document types, schema registry, generation, JSON/YAML output. |
| `route_info.go` | `RouteInfo`, `RouteOptions`, `RouteParameter`, `RouteResponse`. |
| `version.go` | `Version`, parsing, path extraction, `RequireVersion`, `DeprecateVersion`. |
| `middleware.go` | `HandlerFunc`, `Middleware`. |
| `mime.go` | MIME constants used by negotiation and responses. |
| `empty.go` | `Empty` marker type. |
| `internal/radix/tree.go` | Radix tree insertion, lookup, wildcard handling. |
| `internal/radix/node.go` | Node types and child management. |
| `internal/binding/binding.go` | Content-type binders and form mapping. |
| `internal/negotiate/negotiate.go` | RFC 9110 Accept parsing and selection. |
| `middleware/*.go` | The nine middleware implementations. |
| `plugins/*/` | Separate modules; each has its own README and `go.mod`. |
| `examples/*/` | Runnable examples, each its own module. |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Released and unreleased changes. |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Workflow and quality requirements. |

## Summary for AI Agents

1. **Read `CHANGELOG.md` for the current version.** Do not hardcode a version; this file intentionally does not.
2. **Use `Handle` for plain handlers and the uppercase verbs for typed handlers.** They are not interchangeable.
3. **Use `fursy.Empty` for bodyless request or response types.** A non-empty `Req` requires a body.
4. **Let the framework bind and validate.** Do not call `Bind` manually in a typed handler; `ReqBody` is ready.
5. **Return `fursy.Problem` for RFC 9457 errors.** `Box.BadRequest` and friends write typed JSON, not Problems.
6. **Read params, query, and headers from `Context`, not from the body struct.**
7. **Never retain a `Context` or `Box`.** They are pooled and reset.
8. **Register `Recovery` and `Logger` first, `CORS` and `Secure` before `Timeout`, and `CORS` before auth.**
9. **Keep the 4 MiB body limit in mind** and raise it deliberately with `SetMaxBodySize`.
10. **Run `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, and `golangci-lint run` before proposing a change.**
11. **Prefer `go doc -all .` and the examples over memory** when the API is in doubt.
12. **Update `CHANGELOG.md` and the relevant README when behavior or the public API changes.**
